Subject: Performance SLO + customer-led load test coordination (FinWise)

Hey Sam, thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of targets you mentioned:
- P95 latency target: <= 350ms for single-request streaming responses
- Sustainable throughput: 500 qps sustained for peak windows, 2k burst
- Concurrent users: up to 1500 concurrent connections during peak
- Streaming requirement: server-side streaming with chunk size ~256 tokens, end-to-end latency target <= 1s for first chunk

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) You run a customer-led load test (k6 or Locust) against our dedicated test endpoint.
2) We provide a test account, IP allowlist, and a k6 starter script.
3) We monitor on our side (logs, tracing, per-token latency) and share results.

If that sounds good I'll loop in Logan (load-test lead) and Aditya (security/ops) to schedule a window and get the allowlist/test account out to you.

Also attaching a short test-plan draft; will iterate once we confirm the exact script and window.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — that capture looks right. A couple clarifications from our infra team: 
- The 500 qps sustained is our baseline for read-heavy traffic; we may ramp to 1k sustained for a short 30-minute validation.
- Streaming: we care about time-to-first-chunk for user-perceived latency; 1s target is reasonable.
- Auth: we'll use bearer token for tests; do you have short-lived tokens for test accounts?

Preferred test window: next Tuesday 4/12 between 10:00-13:00 PST (we can also do off-hours if that helps).

Can you send the starter k6 script and any IPs to allowlist? We'll run from our k6 cluster (IPs are dynamic but come from the 52.28.0.0/16 and 34.210.0.0/16 pools — we can pin a NAT if needed).

Happy to jump on a quick 15-min call if needed.

Sam

Hi all, quick notes from security/ops side: 
1) IP allowlist: we can add the two CIDR ranges Sam provided to a temporary allowlist for the test window. If FinWise can provide a static NAT IP we'll prefer that; otherwise we'll allow the CIDRs for a limited time.
2) Test account: we will create a short-lived API key scoped to the test endpoint, valid for the 4/12 window + 24h. Credentials will be shared via a secure text file (I'll CC the SSO ticket).
3) Rate-limits: we'll put the test endpoint into a test-mode which relaxes per-user rate limits and enables additional telemetry. This will be timeboxed to the agreed window.
4) Observability: please include the request IDs (x-request-id) in the k6 script so we can match on our side for latency breakdowns.

I'll create the ticket and post the allowlist/update in the shared drive link.

Thanks — I've put together a starter k6 script and a brief runbook. Highlights:
- Script simulates steady-state 500 vus with a ramp to 1000 vus over 15m, then short spike to 2k for 5m for burst validation.
- Auth: uses bearer token env var (K6_TOKEN).
- Headers: script sets x-request-id and chunk-size hint header.
- Metrics: emits timing for time-to-first-chunk and per-chunk durations.

I'm attaching finwise-k6-script.js and the runbook (finwise-load-test-plan.pdf). Please confirm the 4/12 10:00-13:00 PST window; if FinWise wants earlier off-hours we can do 4/13 01:00-04:00 PST as a backup.

Sam, if you can confirm the NAT IP or accept CIDR allowlisting, we'll ask Aditya to add it and then push test creds. Once you receive creds, please run a short smoke (5-10m at low VUs) and share logs/metrics so we can baseline.
